title: Two letters that ask you to stop and listen.
subtitle: Ha Mim opens a surah about hearing
then: This surah came in Makkah while the leaders of Quraysh were trying to talk the Prophet ﷺ out of his mission. It opens with two letters, Ha Mim. {idea}Their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} What they do for the listener is clear: they make you stop.
now: You open the app between two notifications. Your thumb is ready to scroll. Two letters sit there that you cannot explain. {idea}Let them slow you down before the words that follow.{/idea}
old: If I cannot understand something right away, I move past it.
new: Not knowing everything is a reason to listen more carefully, not less.
try: Before you read your next passage of Quran, put the phone face down and take three slow breaths.

title: The message comes from mercy, twice named.
subtitle: Who sent this book, and in what spirit
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the Quran is sent down from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Before any warning, before any story, {reward}the sender is named by His mercy.{/reward} The first people who heard it were mostly hostile, yet it opened with kindness.
now: A letter from a doctor and a letter from someone who loves you can say the same thing. You read them differently. {reward}This one begins by telling you who wrote it and how He feels toward you.{/reward}
old: Religion is mostly about what I am told to do.
new: Every instruction in this book comes wrapped in mercy from the One who sent it.
try: Next time you read a hard verse, remind yourself it was sent by the Most Merciful, then read it again.

title: A book made clear for people who want to know.
subtitle: Detailed verses, plain Arabic, an open door
then: Ibn Kathir says the verses are {idea}clear in meaning and sound in their rulings{/idea}, and the Arabic is precise, not confusing. The Quraysh were masters of Arabic. They understood the words. Clarity was never their problem.
now: You have read long terms and conditions, spreadsheets at work, school forms for your kids. You can understand hard things when you care. {idea}This book is clearer than most of them.{/idea} What it asks is that you come wanting to know.
old: The Quran is too deep for someone like me to understand.
new: It was made clear on purpose, so anyone who sincerely seeks can find their way in.
try: Pick one short verse today, read its translation slowly, and write one sentence on what it says.

title: Good news and warning, and most just turned away.
subtitle: Turning away is how hearing stops
then: Ibn Kathir notes that most of Quraysh {trap}understood nothing of it, even though it was so clear.{/trap} The book carried both hope and warning. They turned their backs, and once you turn away, you stop hearing.
now: Your mother is talking and you are nodding, eyes on the screen. Later you cannot repeat a word she said. {trap}You did not fail to hear. You turned away first.{/trap}
old: If something really mattered, I would notice it.
new: Hearing begins with facing the speaker. If I turn away, even clear words pass me by.
try: In your next real conversation, put the phone away and face the person fully until they finish.

title: Our hearts are covered, they said, so leave us alone.
subtitle: Three walls people build against a message
then: The Quraysh told the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}our hearts are wrapped, our ears are deaf, and there is a screen between us.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains they meant nothing of what he said reached them. So go your way, and we will go ours.
now: A friend says something true about your temper. You say, that is just who I am, take it or leave it. {trap}It sounds like honesty. It is a wall.{/trap} You built it so the words would stop reaching you.
old: Some advice just does not work on me, and that is fine.
new: When I say I cannot hear something, I may be describing a wall I put up myself.
try: Think of one piece of advice you keep brushing off. Listen to it again today without replying.

title: Only a man like you, carrying one message: one God.
subtitle: Go straight to Him and ask forgiveness

picture.label: What he was told to say

then: After their wall of refusal, the Prophet ﷺ is told to answer simply: {idea}I am only a human being like you.{/idea} The revelation is that God is One. Ibn Kathir says this means worship Him alone sincerely, and {reward}seek His forgiveness for past sins.{/reward}
now: You have tried a dozen things to feel at peace: a new routine, a new app, a new plan. Each one asks for a little worship. {idea}This verse says: one direction, straight to Him.{/idea} And the door of forgiveness is open for everything before today.
old: I have drifted too far to simply turn back now.
new: The path is straight and the door is forgiveness. Turning back is the whole instruction.
try: Say astaghfirullah slowly three times today, thinking of one specific thing.

title: Those who keep their souls and wealth unpurified.
subtitle: Zakah as cleaning the self, not only the money

row.title: purification
sub: of the heart and the money

then: Ibn Abbas understood zakah here as {idea}purifying the soul, above all from shirk.{/idea} Others took it as the charity of wealth, which was practiced in some form even in Makkah. Ibn Kathir joins both. Those who refused also {trap}denied the Hereafter.{/trap}
now: Payday comes. The money moves fast: rent, bills, one more order. Giving feels like the last thing on the list. {idea}This verse links what you give with how clean your heart is,{/idea} and with whether you really expect to meet your Lord.
old: Charity is a nice extra once my own needs are covered.
new: Giving is how I clean my heart and my wealth, and it shows what I believe about tomorrow.
try: Give a small amount to someone in need today, even if it is very little.

title: Belief plus good deeds, and a reward that never stops.
subtitle: The one investment that is never cut off
then: Right after the warning comes the hope. Mujahid said this reward {reward}will never be cut off or decrease.{/reward} The believers in Makkah were few and pressured. They were promised something no one could take away.
now: The bonus is spent by next month. The praise for your work is forgotten by Friday. The post you were proud of slides down the feed. {reward}Some good you do today never slides down.{/reward}
old: Good things never last, so I should not expect much.
new: Worldly rewards fade, but faith with good deeds earns a reward that is never cut off.
try: Do one quiet good deed today that no one will see or thank you for.

title: You deny the One who made the ground under you?
subtitle: The Creator of the earth has no rivals
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah here {trap}denounces those who worship others{/trap} while He alone is the Creator, Subduer and Controller of everything. The surah turns to creation in detail: the earth first, like a foundation, then the sky like a roof.
now: You stand on a floor, walk on a road, sleep on ground that holds still. Yet your worry goes to your boss, your bank balance, what people think. {idea}The One who made the ground is the One to rely on.{/idea}
old: Some people and things in my life hold real power over my future.
new: The One who made the earth itself has no rivals, so nothing else deserves my reliance.
try: When you feel a worry today, put your hand flat on the floor and remember who made it.

title: Mountains, blessing, and food measured before you arrived.
subtitle: Provision was placed in the earth for you

picture.label: What He placed in the earth

row.title: already measured
sub: I go out to meet it

then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah blessed the earth and gave it the ability to grow crops. Ikrimah and Mujahid said {reward}He placed in every land what suits no other land.{/reward} The provision of its people was measured in.
now: You check prices at the store and wonder how the month will go. Every item in your basket came from soil somewhere. {reward}Its share was measured before you were born.{/reward} Your job is to go out and meet it.
old: If I stop worrying about money for a moment, everything will fall apart.
new: My provision was measured into the earth by Allah. I work for it, but I do not create it.
try: At your next meal, think of where one item on your plate was grown, and thank Allah for it.

title: Sky and earth said: we come willingly.
subtitle: The whole universe answered yes
then: The surah describes the heaven when it was smoke. Allah said to it and to the earth: {idea}come, willingly or unwillingly.{/idea} They both said, {reward}we come willingly.{/reward} The Quraysh were refusing a message that the sky itself had accepted.
now: The alarm for Fajr goes off. You can get up resenting it, or you can get up like someone answering a call. {reward}The sky and the earth chose the willing way.{/reward} You can choose it too.
old: Obeying Allah is something I do because I have to.
new: All of creation answered willingly. I can join that yes instead of being dragged.
try: Pick one prayer today and walk to it as an answer, not a chore.

title: Seven heavens, each with its task, and lamps that guard.
subtitle: The decree of the Mighty, the Knowing
then: The creation story ends with the sky: seven heavens, {idea}each given its command{/idea}, the nearest one decorated with stars that are both beauty and protection. {idea}That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knower.{/idea}
now: You step out of a late shift and look up for once. A few stars push through the city light. {idea}Each one is where it was placed, doing what it was told.{/idea} Your day felt chaotic. The sky above it was not.
old: Life is random, and nothing above me is really in order.
new: Everything above me runs by a decree of the Mighty and Knowing, and so does my life.
try: Tonight, step outside for one minute and look at the sky before you sleep.

title: If they still turn away, remind them of Ad and Thamud.
subtitle: A warning drawn from nations before
then: After the signs of creation, the Prophet ﷺ is told: if they turn away, say {trap}I have warned you of a punishment like the one that struck Ad and Thamud.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says these nations disbelieved in their messengers. The warning was meant to wake people, not to scare for its own sake.
now: You read news of a company that collapsed after years of ignoring warnings. You think, they should have listened. {idea}The verse asks you to turn that thought on yourself{/idea}: which warning in your own life are you ignoring?
old: Stories of destroyed nations are about other people, long ago.
new: Those stories are told so that I check my own heart while there is still time.
try: Name one warning sign in your own habits that you have been ignoring, and take one step on it.

title: Messengers came from every side, and they wanted angels instead.
subtitle: Rejecting the message because of the messenger
then: Ibn Kathir says messengers were sent to the towns around Ad and Thamud, bringing good news and warnings. The people answered: {trap}if Allah wanted, He would have sent angels. You are only men like us.{/trap} They judged the carrier and ignored the message.
now: Your younger cousin reminds you to pray. A coworker you dislike says something wise. Your first thought is, who are you to tell me. {trap}The message gets lost in the messenger.{/trap} {idea}The truth does not change with the voice that carries it.{/idea}
old: I will listen when the right kind of person says it.
new: A true reminder deserves my attention no matter who brings it to me.
try: Think of one good reminder you dismissed because of who said it. Act on it today.

title: Who is stronger than us? The One who made you.
subtitle: The arrogance of Ad and their strength
then: Ad were arrogant in the land without right. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they boasted of their physical strength and thought it would protect them.{/trap} The verse asks: did they not see that {idea}Allah who created them, and gave them that strength, is stronger still?{/idea}
now: You are young, healthy, earning well. You skip the checkup and the prayer and think, I am fine. {trap}Strength makes us feel untouchable.{/trap} {idea}Every bit of it was given, and can be taken in one afternoon.{/idea}
old: As long as I am strong and capable, I can handle whatever comes.
new: My strength is on loan from the One who made me, and He is far stronger.
try: Thank Allah today for one specific strength you have, by name.

title: A cold, roaring wind for those proud of their strength.
subtitle: Disgrace in this world, more in the next
then: Ibn Kathir says the wind was strong, cold and loud, {idea}a fitting answer to a people deceived by their physical strength.{/idea} It lasted days in succession. The disgrace in this world was {trap}small beside the disgrace of the Hereafter.{/trap}
now: You have watched someone lose everything quickly: a business, a reputation, their health. It rarely comes from where they were guarding. {idea}The verse points you at your own pride{/idea}, not at anyone else's fall.
old: I have covered every risk, so nothing can really hurt me.
new: Pride guards the wrong door. Humility before Allah is the only real safety.
try: Name one area where you feel too sure of yourself, and make a short dua for humility in it.

title: Thamud were shown the way and chose blindness.
subtitle: Guidance was clear, and they preferred the dark
then: Ibn Abbas and others said Allah {idea}explained the truth to Thamud{/idea} through their Prophet Salih. Ibn Kathir says they opposed him and slaughtered the she-camel, the sign sent to them. {trap}They loved blindness more than guidance.{/trap}
now: You know the late-night scrolling is hurting your sleep and your prayer. You have read the advice. You keep the phone by the bed. {trap}It is not that you cannot see.{/trap} Sometimes you prefer not to look.
old: I would change if I only knew better.
new: Often I already know. The real question is whether I love the guidance more than the habit.
try: Pick one habit you know is harmful and make it a little harder to reach tonight.

title: In the middle of the ruin, the believers were saved.
subtitle: Faith and fear of Allah carried them out
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah saved the believers {reward}along with their Prophet Salih, and no harm came to them,{/reward} because they feared Allah. They were few, living among people who mocked them. The early Muslims in Makkah heard this and recognized themselves.
now: You are the only one at the office who steps away to pray. The only one in the family group who does not share the gossip. It can feel lonely. {reward}This verse is about the few who held on and were carried through.{/reward}
old: If I am the only one doing what is right, maybe I am the one who is wrong.
new: Being few never made the believers lose. Their faith and fear of Allah carried them out.
try: Keep one good practice today even if no one around you does it.

title: Remember the Day the enemies of Allah are gathered.
subtitle: From history to the Day that is coming
then: After the stories of Ad and Thamud, the surah turns to the future. Ibn Kathir says this was a reminder to the idolators of Makkah of {trap}the Day they would be gathered, the first of them with the last.{/trap} The past nations were gone. This Day was still ahead.
now: You read about old nations like history homework. Then the verse closes the book and points to a date on your own calendar. {idea}Not their Day. Yours.{/idea} The good news: it has not come yet.
old: Judgment is a story about other people's endings.
new: Every story of the past points at my own Day, which is still ahead and still open.
try: Ask yourself tonight: if today were recorded in full, what would I want it to show? Then do one thing.

title: Your ears, eyes and skin will tell what you did.
subtitle: The body as a witness
then: When they reach the edge of the Fire, their own hearing, sight and skin bear witness. Ibn Kathir says this covers {trap}all their deeds, earlier and later; not a single letter concealed.{/trap} The idolators in Makkah thought private sins were private.
now: Your door is locked. The screen is at an angle no one can see. You think it is just you. {idea}Your eyes are there. Your hands are there.{/idea} The witnesses go everywhere you go.
old: What I do in private stays between me and nobody.
new: There is no private place. My own body is a witness to everything I do.
try: Before one private moment today, pause and ask: would I be at peace if my eyes spoke of this?

title: Why did you speak against us? Allah made us speak.
subtitle: When the body answers its owner
then: Ibn Kathir records a hadith where the Prophet ﷺ smiled at how a servant will argue with his Lord, {trap}accepting no witness except from himself.{/trap} Then his mouth is sealed and {idea}his limbs speak.{/idea} He turns on them: it was for you that I argued.
now: You defend your choices hard: in arguments, in your head, in long messages explaining yourself. You think your body is on your side. {idea}It belongs to the One who made it the first time.{/idea}
old: My body is mine, and it will always back me up.
new: My limbs were created by Allah and will speak by His command. They are a trust, not my lawyers.
try: Use your hands for one act of kindness today that you would be glad for them to report.

title: You did not hide, because you thought He did not know.
subtitle: A whispered conversation behind the Kaaba
then: Abdullah said he was hiding under the covering of the Kaaba when three men came by. One asked, {trap}does Allah hear what we say?{/trap} Another said, only if we raise our voices. The third said, {idea}if He hears one thing, He hears everything.{/idea} Then this verse came down.
now: You would never say a harsh word in front of your parents. But in a whisper to a friend, in a deleted message, in a quiet thought, you do. {trap}Somewhere inside is the idea that quiet things count less.{/trap}
old: Allah sees the big things, but the small and quiet ones slip past.
new: If He hears anything, He hears everything. My whisper is as clear to Him as my shout.
try: Notice one thing you say quietly today that you would not say aloud, and drop it.

title: One wrong thought about your Lord can ruin you.
subtitle: What you assume about Allah shapes your life
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}their evil thought, that Allah did not know much of what they did,{/trap} is what doomed them. The deeds came from the belief. They lost themselves and their families on the Day.
now: How you picture your boss shapes how you work. How you picture a friend shapes how you treat them. {idea}How you picture Allah shapes everything.{/idea} A careless thought about Him becomes a careless life.
old: What I think about Allah in my head does not change much in real life.
new: My assumptions about my Lord drive my deeds. Getting Him right comes first.
try: Learn one of Allah's names today, like Al-Alim, the All-Knowing, and say it in your dua.

title: When the chance to make amends has passed.
subtitle: Excuses that come too late
then: Ibn Kathir says on that Day, {trap}whether they bear it patiently or not, there is no escape.{/trap} Ibn Jarir says they will ask to be sent back to the world, and the plea will not be answered. The verse was a warning to people who still had time.
now: You keep saying you will fix things with your brother, start praying properly, return what you owe. Someday. {reward}Right now, every apology is still accepted.{/reward} The verse is about a door that closes, so you walk through it while it is open.
old: There will always be time to make it right later.
new: Seeking Allah's pleasure is accepted now. There is a point when it will not be.
try: Do the one making-amends you have been putting off: a call, a message, or a prayer.

title: Close companions who made wrong look right.
subtitle: Choose who stands beside you
then: Ibn Kathir says these companions {trap}made their past deeds look good to them, and their future too{/trap}, so they only saw themselves as doing well. He links it to the verse that whoever turns from Allah's remembrance gets a devil for a companion.
now: The friend who always says you deserve it. The feed that tells you everyone is doing it. The voice that turns a bad night into a funny story. {trap}Companions decorate.{/trap} {idea}Notice who is decorating your choices.{/idea}
old: I make my own choices; the people around me do not change that.
new: My companions make some things look beautiful. I need ones who make the right things look beautiful.
try: Spend ten minutes today with someone, or something, that reminds you of Allah.

title: Do not listen, make noise over it, and you will win.
subtitle: The strategy of drowning out the Quran
then: Mujahid explained that the Quraysh would {trap}whistle and make noise to confuse the Prophet ﷺ when he recited.{/trap} They feared what would happen if people really heard it. Ibn Kathir says Allah commands the opposite: {reward}listen and be silent, that you may receive mercy.{/reward}
now: You put on a recitation and leave the TV on, the chat open, the earbuds half in. {trap}You do not mean to drown it out, but the noise wins.{/trap} The Quran was always meant to be heard in silence.
old: Having the Quran on in the background is enough.
new: The Quran asks for my silence. Listening fully is where its mercy reaches me.
try: Listen to one short surah today with nothing else on, eyes closed if you can.

title: Fighting the message carries a heavy cost.
subtitle: The answer to drowning out the Quran
then: Ibn Kathir says this punishment comes {trap}in return for what they did when they heard the Quran{/trap}, and for their evil deeds. Shouting over the message was not a joke to Allah. It was a choice with weight.
now: Mocking a reminder, rolling your eyes at a lecture, changing the subject when someone talks about Allah. {trap}It feels small.{/trap} {idea}The verse says how we treat His words matters a great deal.{/idea} That cuts both ways: honoring them matters too.
old: Brushing off religious talk is just a reaction, not a real deed.
new: How I respond to Allah's words is itself a deed, and it carries weight with Him.
try: The next time a reminder comes up, let the person finish and say thank you.

title: The end of those who kept rejecting His signs.
subtitle: What denial leads to, stated plainly
then: This verse closes the passage about those who drowned out the Quran. Ibn Kathir calls it {trap}the recompense of the enemies of Allah, for denying His signs.{/trap} The listeners in Makkah were being told plainly where their path ended while they could still leave it.
now: A doctor tells you where a habit is heading, not to scare you but so you change. {idea}This verse is that kind of honesty.{/idea} The question is not about anyone else. It is which signs you have been brushing aside.
old: Talk of the Fire is meant to frighten, not to help.
new: Being told the end of a road is a mercy, because it lets me choose a different road today.
try: Ask Allah tonight to protect you from the Fire, and name one thing you will change for it.

title: Show us who misled us, so we can blame them.
subtitle: Followers turn on those they followed
then: Ali said those who led them astray were {trap}Iblis and the son of Adam who killed his brother{/trap}, the first to start shirk and the first to start murder. The followers want them crushed beneath. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse where {idea}each one gets what they deserve.{/idea}
now: It was the friends. It was the way I was raised. It was the influencer I followed. {trap}There is some truth in that.{/trap} But on the Day, pointing does not carry you. {idea}You still chose whom to follow.{/idea}
old: If someone led me into it, most of the blame is theirs.
new: Those who mislead carry their share, but I carry mine for following them.
try: Look at who you follow online and unfollow one account that pulls you toward wrong.

title: Say my Lord is Allah, then stand firm.
subtitle: Angels arrive with no fear and no grief
then: A companion asked the Prophet ﷺ for something to hold on to. He said: {idea}say, my Lord is Allah, then stand firm.{/idea} Asked what he feared most, he took hold of his own tongue. Scholars said the angels come at death, telling the believer {reward}do not fear what is ahead, do not grieve for what you leave behind.{/reward}
now: You are in a hospital corridor, or lying awake worried about your kids if something happens to you. {reward}This verse is the promise for that moment.{/reward} The work is simple and long: keep saying it, keep living it.
old: Faith is a strong feeling I either have or do not have.
new: Faith is saying my Lord is Allah and then staying on course, day after ordinary day.
try: Guard your tongue for one full day from one specific thing, like complaining or gossip.

title: We were your friends here, and we still are.
subtitle: The angels were with you all along
then: Ibn Kathir says the angels will tell the believers {reward}we were your close companions in this world, protecting and helping you by Allah's command.{/reward} They will be with them in the grave, at the Trumpet, and across the bridge. And in Paradise, whatever they wish for will be theirs.
now: You moved to a new city. Your phone is quiet on a Friday night. You feel invisible. {reward}The believer was never as alone as they felt.{/reward} Companions sent by Allah were there the whole time.
old: When no one calls, it means I am truly alone.
new: A believer is never alone. Allah's angels are friends in this life and the next.
try: On your next lonely moment, make dua and remember you are being kept company.

title: A welcome prepared by the Forgiving, the Merciful.
subtitle: Paradise as hospitality from your Host
then: Ibn Kathir explains the word as {reward}a welcoming gift and blessing{/reward} from the One who forgave your sins, {idea}concealed your faults and was kind and merciful.{/idea} The early believers were being treated as outcasts in Makkah. Here they are honored guests.
now: Think of arriving at a relative's home after a long trip: the food ready, the bed made, nobody asking what took you so long. {reward}That is the picture.{/reward} The Host already knows your faults and has covered them.
old: If I ever get to Paradise, I will feel like I squeezed in.
new: The believers are welcomed like guests by a Host who forgives and covers their faults.
try: Host someone today, even with tea, and remember how Allah welcomes His guests.

title: The best words: inviting to Allah and living it.
subtitle: Speech backed by deeds
then: Ibn Kathir says this person {idea}follows what he says, so it benefits him and others.{/idea} He is not one who enjoins good and does not do it. Al-Hasan Al-Basri called such a person beloved to Allah. The Prophet ﷺ is the first example.
now: You share a reminder in the family group chat. Then you snap at your sister over dinner. {trap}People notice the gap.{/trap} {reward}The best invitation to Allah is a life that matches the words.{/reward}
old: Calling people to good is for scholars and speakers, not for me.
new: Anyone who lives what they say and invites others gently is speaking the best words.
try: Before sharing a reminder today, do the thing it asks yourself first.

title: Answer harm with something better, and an enemy can become a friend.
subtitle: Good and bad are never equal
then: Umar said: {idea}there is no better punishment for one who disobeys Allah about you than your obeying Allah about him.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says treating well those who treat you badly leads to {reward}reconciliation, love and empathy.{/reward} This was said to believers being insulted daily in Makkah.
now: Your coworker took credit for your work. The neighbor parks across your driveway again. Your hand is already typing the reply. {idea}Answer with something better.{/idea} You may be surprised who becomes a friend.
old: If I am kind to someone who hurt me, they will walk all over me.
new: Answering harm with good is strength. It can turn an enemy into a close friend.
try: Do one kind thing today for someone who has been unkind to you.

title: Only the patient reach this, those with a great share.
subtitle: Returning good for harm is a gift
then: Ibn Kathir admits {idea}this advice is difficult for people{/idea}, so only the patient act on it. Ibn Abbas said Allah commands patience in anger, forbearance with ignorance, and forgiveness when mistreated. Then {reward}Allah protects them and softens their enemies.{/reward}
now: It is hard. Your face is hot, your heart is racing, the comeback is perfect. {idea}Holding it in for ten seconds is the real test.{/idea} The verse says the ones who manage it have a great portion.
old: Some people are just calm by nature; I am not one of them.
new: Repelling harm with good is a skill grown through patience, and Allah gives a great share to those who try.
try: Next time you feel anger rise today, count to ten before speaking.

title: When Shaytan nudges you, run to Allah.
subtitle: Some whispers cannot be handled with kindness
then: Ibn Kathir says a human enemy may be won over by kindness, but {trap}the whispers of Shaytan cannot be dealt with{/trap} except by seeking refuge with Allah. The Prophet ﷺ would begin his prayer by {idea}seeking refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from Shaytan.{/idea}
now: You have just decided to forgive. Then a voice in your head replays the insult, louder each time. {trap}That is not a person to be reasoned with.{/trap} {idea}Say a'udhu billah and step away.{/idea}
old: I just need to win the argument going on in my head.
new: Some inner voices are whispers to be refused, not debated. Allah hears when I seek refuge.
try: When a bad thought loops today, say a'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim and change rooms.

title: Bow to the Maker of the sun, not the sun.
subtitle: The most beautiful things are still creations
then: Ibn Kathir says the sun and moon are {idea}the most beautiful of the bodies we see{/idea}, so Allah points out that they too are created, under His control. Night and day mark weeks, months, years, worship and rights. {trap}Worship of Him does not benefit if others are worshipped beside Him.{/trap}
now: Nobody bows to the sun today. But you might organize your whole life around a career, a person, a look, a number in the bank. {trap}Beautiful things become what we bow to.{/trap} {idea}Look past them to their Maker.{/idea}
old: Loving something beautiful very deeply cannot be a problem.
new: The most beautiful things are signs. My bowing belongs only to the One who made them.
try: Watch a sunset or sunrise this week and say subhanallah for the One behind it.

title: If they are too proud, the angels never tire.
subtitle: Allah does not need our worship
then: Ibn Kathir says if they are too proud to worship Allah alone, {idea}the angels with your Lord glorify Him night and day without tiring.{/idea} He compares it to the verse where Allah entrusts His message to another people if one rejects it. This is a verse of prostration.
now: You skip a prayer and feel, somewhere inside, like you made a point. {idea}Allah lost nothing.{/idea} Countless angels glorified Him in that same minute. {reward}You were the one who missed out.{/reward}
old: My worship is something I give to Allah.
new: Allah is glorified without end. My worship is a gift He gives me, not one I give Him.
try: Make one sajdah today slowly, staying a little longer than usual.

title: Dead earth stirs with rain, and so will the dead.
subtitle: A sign of resurrection outside your window
then: Ibn Kathir says this is a sign of {idea}His ability to bring the dead back to life.{/idea} The earth is lifeless, then rain comes and it brings forth crops and fruit. The Quraysh doubted resurrection. The answer was in their own fields after rain.
now: A dry patch of grass by the bus stop turns green after a week of rain. A plant you forgot on the windowsill sprouts again. {idea}Your heart can be like that too.{/idea} {reward}What looks dead is not beyond Him.{/reward}
old: Some things in me are too far gone to come back to life.
new: The One who revives dead earth revives the dead, and He can revive a hardened heart.
try: Water a plant today, and make dua for one part of your life that feels dry.

title: Twisting His verses is never hidden from Him.
subtitle: Do what you will; He sees it
then: Ibn Abbas said this twisting means {trap}putting words in their improper places.{/trap} Ibn Kathir calls the verse a stern warning. Mujahid and others said that {idea}do what you will is a threat, not a permission{/idea}, because He sees everything you do.
now: You hear someone bend a verse to fit what they already wanted. You catch yourself doing it too: quoting the easy parts, skipping the hard ones. {idea}He sees the twisting.{/idea} {reward}He also sees the honest reader trying.{/reward}
old: As long as I can find a verse to support me, I am fine.
new: Allah sees whether I follow His words or bend them. I want to arrive on that Day secure.
try: Read one verse today that challenges you, and sit with it instead of explaining it away.

title: They rejected the Reminder, and it is a mighty Book.
subtitle: A protected book no one can match
then: Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi and Qatadah said the Reminder here {idea}is the Quran.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it is {idea}protected and preserved, and nobody can produce anything like it.{/idea} Quraysh rejected it, but rejection did nothing to its standing.
now: A book has sat on your shelf for years, the cover dusty. You meant to read it properly. {idea}It has not lost anything by waiting.{/idea} The only one missing out is the person who keeps not opening it.
old: If I ignore the Quran, it does not really matter much.
new: The Quran stays mighty whether I read it or not. Ignoring it only costs me.
try: Open a physical or digital mushaf today and read one page.

title: Falsehood cannot reach it from front or back.
subtitle: Sent down by the Wise, the Praiseworthy
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}there is no way to corrupt it{/idea}, because it came from the Lord of the worlds. He is Wise in all He says and does, and {reward}Praiseworthy in all He commands and forbids.{/reward}
now: Your feed shows a story, then a correction, then a correction of the correction. Edited photos, rewritten history, deleted posts. {reward}In all that noise, there is one text that falsehood cannot get into.{/reward}
old: Everything is spin; nothing I read can be fully trusted.
new: The Quran is guarded from falsehood on every side. I can rest my trust there.
try: Replace five minutes of news scrolling today with five minutes of Quran.

title: Every insult you hear, messengers before you heard too.
subtitle: Comfort for the rejected, and a Lord of forgiveness
then: Qatadah and As-Suddi said: {idea}nothing is said to you by way of rejection that was not said to the messengers before you.{/idea} As they bore insults with patience, so must you. Then a balance: your Lord {reward}forgives those who turn to Him{/reward}, and punishes those who persist.
now: You try to do the right thing and someone mocks you for it. A family member calls you extreme for praying on time. {idea}You are not the first. You are walking an old road.{/idea}
old: If people mock me for my faith, I must be doing something wrong.
new: Mockery for doing right is an old pattern. Messengers faced it, and patience is the answer.
try: The next time someone mocks a good habit of yours, answer calmly and keep doing it.

title: For believers, guidance and cure; for others, a distant call.
subtitle: The same words, two very different effects
then: Ibn Kathir says their rejection was {trap}the disbelief of stubbornness.{/trap} Had it come in a foreign language, they would have complained it was not Arabic. For a believer it is {reward}guidance for the heart and a cure for doubts.{/reward} Mujahid said the distant place is far from their hearts.
now: Two people sit through the same Friday talk. One leaves lighter, a doubt settled. The other says it was too long. {idea}The words were the same. The hearts were not.{/idea}
old: If the reminder were delivered better, it would reach me.
new: The Quran heals the heart that comes to it in faith. Distance is in the listener, not the words.
try: Bring one real doubt or worry to the Quran today and read a passage with it in mind.

title: Musa's people argued over their book too.
subtitle: A delay that is a mercy, not a forgetting
then: Ibn Kathir says Musa's people {trap}disputed his Scripture and showed him no respect{/trap}, just as Quraysh did with the Prophet ﷺ. Had a word not gone before from Allah, {idea}delaying the reckoning to an appointed term{/idea}, it would have been settled already.
now: You did something wrong and nothing happened. A week passed, then a month. {trap}It is easy to think it did not matter.{/trap} {idea}The delay is time given, not a sign that no one noticed.{/idea}
old: If nothing bad happened after I did wrong, it must not have mattered.
new: Allah's delay is a mercy with a deadline. It is space for me to turn back.
try: Think of one wrong that seemed to have no consequence, and seek forgiveness for it today.

title: Your good is for you, your harm is against you.
subtitle: And your Lord is never unjust
then: Ibn Kathir says the benefit of a good deed {reward}comes back to the one who did it{/reward}, and so do the consequences of evil. Allah {idea}punishes no one except after establishing proof and sending a messenger.{/idea}
now: You hold the door for a stranger, help your kid with homework, pray when you are tired. It feels like giving away. {reward}It is all landing in your own account.{/reward} So is the sharp reply you send at midnight.
old: When I do good, I am mostly doing it for others.
new: Every good deed is a gift to my own soul, and every harm I do lands on me too.
try: Do one good deed today and quietly remind yourself it is for your own soul.

title: He knows the Hour, every fruit, every birth.
subtitle: Nothing grows or is born outside His knowledge
then: When Jibril asked about the Hour, the Prophet ﷺ said {idea}the one asked knows no more than the one asking.{/idea} Ibn Kathir adds that every fruit from its sheath and every pregnancy is in His knowledge. On the Day, those who worshipped others will say {trap}none of us bears witness to any partner.{/trap}
now: You are waiting outside a delivery room, or for test results, or for a harvest of a different kind: a job offer, an answer. {idea}He already knows every detail of what is coming.{/idea} You can hand Him the waiting.
old: I need to know what is coming before I can feel calm.
new: He knows every birth, every fruit, every hour. My calm can rest on His knowing.
try: Name one thing you are anxiously waiting for and give it to Allah in a short dua.

title: What they called on before simply disappears.
subtitle: False supports leave when you need them
then: Ibn Kathir says those they used to invoke {trap}will go away and be of no benefit to them.{/trap} The idolators of Makkah trusted their idols to intercede. On the Day, there would be no refuge from what they had done.
now: You lean on a habit to cope: a show, a snack, a scroll. It is there every night. {trap}Then the real crisis comes and it has nothing to offer.{/trap} {reward}The verse asks what will still be there when everything else leaves.{/reward}
old: The things I rely on will be there when I really need them.
new: Only Allah remains when every other support disappears. He is the one to lean on now.
try: Next time you reach for a comfort habit today, make a short dua first.

title: Never tired of asking, quick to lose hope.
subtitle: How we swing between wanting and despair
then: Ibn Kathir says man {idea}never gets bored of asking for good things{/idea} like wealth and health, but when trial or poverty touches him, he {trap}thinks he will never experience anything good again.{/trap} The verse describes a pattern, not one person.
now: Your duas are long when you want a promotion. Then the rejection email arrives, and you close the prayer mat for a month. {trap}One hard week and you decide nothing will ever go right.{/trap}
old: When something goes wrong, it proves nothing good is coming.
new: Hardship is not the end of good. The same Lord I asked yesterday is there today.
try: If something has gone wrong this week, make one dua for good anyway, today.

title: Relief comes, and he says: I earned this.
subtitle: Taking credit for mercy

row.title: and if there is a Lord
sub: He will be good to me

then: Ibn Kathir says when good comes after difficulty, he says {trap}this is because of me, I deserve this.{/trap} He doubts the Hour, yet assumes if it comes, Allah will treat him well anyway. Ibn Kathir links this to the verse that {trap}man transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient.{/trap}
now: The job finally comes through after months of searching. Within a week you are telling people it was your interview skills. {trap}The months of dua are forgotten.{/trap} {reward}It was a taste of mercy.{/reward}
old: When things finally go well, it is because I worked for it.
new: Every relief after hardship is a mercy tasted from Allah, not a wage I earned.
try: Think of one good thing that came after a hard time and thank Allah for it by name.

title: Blessed, he turns away; in trouble, he prays at length.
subtitle: Remembering Allah only in emergencies
then: Ibn Kathir says when given favor, man {trap}turns away from obedience and is too proud.{/trap} When difficulty touches him, he makes long supplications, {trap}long on words, short on meaning.{/trap} He links it to the verse of the man who prays lying, sitting and standing, then forgets once the harm is lifted.
now: In the hospital waiting room you pray like never before. Two weeks after the all-clear, you are back to skipping Fajr. {idea}The verse is not mocking the dua. It is asking you to keep it going.{/idea}
old: I will turn to Allah seriously when I really need Him.
new: I need Him in the good days too. Remembering Him in ease keeps me close in hardship.
try: Make a dua of thanks today for something that is going well right now.

title: What if it really is from Allah?
subtitle: A question worth sitting with
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask the deniers: {idea}tell me, if this Quran is from Allah and you reject it, what is your position?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says such a person is in {trap}stubborn opposition, on a path far from guidance.{/trap}
now: You would not ignore a letter from the bank that says your account is at risk, just in case it is real. {idea}Ask the same honest question about the Quran.{/idea} What if every word is true?
old: I can put off taking the Quran seriously until I am sure.
new: If it is from Allah, then ignoring it is the biggest risk I could take.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: if every verse is true, what one thing would I change?

title: Signs on the horizons and inside yourselves.
subtitle: Proof outside and within, and Allah as Witness
then: Mujahid and others said the signs included events like {idea}Badr and the conquest of Makkah{/idea}, which the Quraysh lived through. Ibn Kathir adds it may mean {idea}the human body and its design{/idea}, showing the Creator's wisdom. And {reward}Allah is enough as a Witness.{/reward}
now: Your heartbeat, without you asking. The way your cut healed by itself. The turn in your life you never planned. {idea}Signs, inside and around you.{/idea} You have been reading them all along without noticing.
old: I would believe more firmly if I saw a clear sign.
new: Signs are already in the world and in my own body. Allah is witness over everything.
try: Put your hand on your chest for a minute today, feel your heartbeat, and say alhamdulillah.

title: In doubt about meeting their Lord, who surrounds everything.
subtitle: The surah ends with the meeting ahead
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}did not think about the Hour or strive for it; they regarded it as irrelevant.{/trap} But it will come. The surah ends saying {idea}all of creation is under His control and knowledge{/idea}, so bringing the Hour is easy for Him.
now: You plan the holiday, the next career step, the kids' schooling. The one meeting that is certain gets no planning at all. {idea}The surah ends by placing it back on your calendar.{/idea}
old: Meeting Allah is far off; I will think about it later.
new: The meeting with my Lord is certain, and He surrounds everything, including my today.
try: Spend two minutes tonight thinking about meeting Allah, and what you hope to bring.
